questions.prompt: The family gets the room ready one hour before the guests arrive. Which action do they do?

options.text: They put on their best clothes.

questions.explanation: Making the room ready with flowers, lights and paper is called decorating it. Waiting for midnight happens at the very end of the evening, hugging each other is something people do to one another and not to the room, and putting on your best clothes gets a person ready, not a place.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: "My little brother ___ the right to clothing and to health."
questions.explanation: My little brother is one boy, that is he, and with he, she or it the verb becomes has: he has the right to clothing. The form "have" belongs to I, you, we and they, "having" cannot be the verb of the sentence on its own, and "are" would need a completely different structure.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: "Last Friday, the pupils ___ a show for their teacher."
questions.explanation: Last Friday is a finished moment, so the verb goes to the simple past, and prepare ends in e, so it takes only -d. The forms "prepare" and "prepares" stay in the present, and "will prepare" points to the future, which last Friday forbids.

questions.prompt: Which of these past forms is written correctly?
questions.explanation: The verb stop is short and ends in one vowel plus one consonant, so the p doubles before the ending: stopped. The spelling "stoped" forgets the doubling, "stopeed" invents an e the verb does not have, and "stoppd" drops the e of the ending.

questions.prompt: Complete both blanks: "Last night we ___ lemonade and we ___ our snacks together."
questions.explanation: Both verbs are irregular and change shape instead of taking an ending: drink becomes drank and eat becomes ate. The forms "drinked" and "eated" glue the regular ending to verbs that refuse it, and the two mixed pairs get one verb right and the other wrong.

questions.prompt: Karim reads the verb helped aloud. How does its final -ed sound?
questions.explanation: The verb help ends in the quiet sound p, where your throat stays still, so the ending of helped is the quiet /t/. The buzzing /d/ needs a sound that shakes the throat, the syllable /ɪd/ needs a verb that ends in t or d, and /z/ is the ending of plays, a present form.
